findings.how_to_check: Examine demographic characteristics (race, nativity, literacy, name commonness) of records in mlp_training1930_1940.dta relative to the full 1940 census sample; verify whether census names were used in constructing unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930.dta and 1940.dta.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel 'Verified Correct' to 'Agrees with FamilySearch Reference' or 'Genealogical Match' in table rows and prose, and explicitly discuss sample selection and circularity risks in the paper's methodology section.
findings.title: FamilySearch profile sample is treated as ground truth and labeled 'Verified Correct'
findings.what_the_code_does: The updated constants in MATCHING/score_fs_links.do score proposed census links against 'A'S COMPLETE TRUTH FILE' (lines 46-47), counting links as verified where person_merge == 3 & histid1930 == true_histid1930 (line 217) and writing 'Verified Correct' into the LaTeX results table (line 392). However, CODE/create_linked_sample_for_MLP_training.do:5-15 shows this benchmark is constructed by inner-merging 1930 and 1940 FamilySearch-profile crosswalks and retaining only profiles with complete, ordered vital dates (birthyr, deathyr, birthmon, deathmon). The code treats agreement with a selected genealogical sample as ground truth.
findings.why_it_matters: Individuals linked across censuses on FamilySearch user trees with complete vital dates are unrepresentative of the 1940 census population, skewing toward native-born, literate, and demographically stable households where transcription errors are least prevalent. Furthermore, if census names guided the initial profile attachment, evaluating name-based linkage against them is partially circular. Presenting these rates as 'Verified Correct' rather than agreement with a genealogical benchmark invites referee skepticism.

findings.how_to_check: Compare line 376 of MATCHING/score_fs_links.do with LINKAGE/notes/truth_file_provenance.md:32-36 and replication/README.md:80.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'MLP genealogical links' to 'FamilySearch-profile reference sample' in MATCHING/score_fs_links.do lines 15 and 376.
findings.title: Generated LaTeX table note and code comments attribute reference links to IPUMS MLP rather than FamilySearch profiles
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 15 comments that truth is 'the MLP genealogical links', and line 376 writes directly into the output LaTeX table MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex: '% Verified/Unverifiable/Contradicted are against the MLP genealogical links, as in the paper.'. However, the project's provenance resolution in LINKAGE/notes/truth_file_provenance.md:32-36 and replication/README.md:80 established that mlp_training1930_1940.dta is not an IPUMS MLP crosswalk extraction, but Sam Hwang's FamilySearch tree profile sample built by CODE/create_linked_sample_for_MLP_training.do.
findings.why_it_matters: The output file MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex is an artifact generated for publication. Emitting a comment attributing the benchmark to the MLP crosswalk propagates an inaccurate provenance claim that has already been corrected elsewhere in repository documentation.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied (PaperPath not provided); claims-vs-code review could not verify manuscript text, prose claims, or numbers reported in the draft.

External datasets on drives F: and D: were not accessible and the Stata pipeline could not be executed; review of numerical and runtime behavior relies on analytical tracing and repository documentation.

The generation scripts for unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930.dta and 1940.dta reside outside this repository, preventing verification of whether census names contributed to upstream profile attachment.
Commit 3ca56d2 cited in MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:47 belongs to an external paper repository not resolvable from this working tree.
structured_output.summary: The working-tree change in MATCHING/score_fs_links.do correctly updates the regression gating constants to match Machine A's complete truth file, exhibiting exact internal arithmetic consistency and proper assertion gates that halt execution on divergence. However, the script and its generated LaTeX output table continue to mislabel the benchmark as 'the MLP genealogical links' and describe agreement with this selected FamilySearch-profile sample as 'Verified Correct'. The key priority is correcting the data provenance note in the output table and explicitly qualifying the genealogical benchmark in the text.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
